basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A specific vehicle instance, not its type, model or variant.
Holds physical composition, capacities and observed state across road, rail, water and air modes.
Registration, approval and maintenance are referenced records, not part of the instance.
Separate from the journey or shipment it performs.

may: Read vehicle identity, specifications and observed state from authorized sources.
Record observations and telemetry with time and source.
Report defects and recall matches to the responsible party.
Check capacity before planning loads or passengers.
mustNot: Operate, unlock or control a vehicle without explicit authorization.
Exceed rated capacities or mass limits in plans.
Track or disclose vehicle location in ways that reveal a person's movements without basis.
Alter odometer, identification or safety configuration records.
Assume a vehicle is roadworthy from its record alone.
requiresHuman: Taking control of a vehicle in operation.
Declaring a vehicle unsafe or taking it out of service.

considerations: Vehicles are a major cause of injury and death, so safety data must be accurate.
Location and driving data reveal personal life and must be protected.
Emissions and noise affect public health.

items: Length, width and height in metres, measured unladen.
Unladen mass and gross vehicle mass in kilograms.
Speed in kilometres per hour or knots as appropriate to the mode.
Energy level as fuel volume in litres or battery state of charge in percent.
Tyre pressure in kilopascals, measured cold.
Odometer reading in kilometres, with date.
A vehicle is recognised by registration plate or marking, VIN or hull number, shape, colour and livery.
It is confused with similar vehicles of the same model, with trailers and with cloned plates.
Fire, especially of fuel or traction batteries.
Unexpected movement during loading or maintenance.
ISO 15118 for electric vehicle charging communication.
